report.summary: Analyzed personas.py module: 3 public functions, 1 private cache, 1 constant. Claims about shadow naming, culture, and roster are partially checkable.
risks: _REGISTRY_PATH | medium | Hardcoded path to personas.json may cause issues if file missing or malformed; no error handling. | Check if personas.json exists and is valid JSON.
persona_for | low | Default fallback returns provider string if no match, which may not be a valid persona name. | Verify that provider default is always a string.
roster | low | Returns list of names but order may vary due to dict.fromkeys; no guarantee of consistency across calls. | Confirm that dict.fromkeys preserves insertion order (Python 3.7+).

handoff.purpose: Provide shadow persona names for different providers (DeepSeek, Ollama) based on a JSON registry.

symbols.name: _REGISTRY_PATH
symbols.note: Path to personas.json in same directory.

symbols.name: _registry
symbols.note: Private cached function that loads and returns the JSON registry as a dict.

symbols.name: persona_for
symbols.note: Returns shadow persona name for a given provider and agent name, falling back to provider default.

symbols.name: culture
symbols.note: Returns culture string for a provider from the registry.

symbols.name: roster
symbols.note: Returns list of all named workers (shadows plus pool) for a provider, deduplicated.

claims.text: Each Claude specialist keeps its name on the trusted Claude lane, but gets a named *shadow* when the same role runs on a cheaper backend: a Chinese name on DeepSeek (external) and a Mexican/Italian name on local Ollama.
claims.why: The code does not reference Claude, DeepSeek, Ollama, Chinese, Mexican, or Italian names. The actual naming conventions are in personas.json, which is not provided.

claims.text: Purely cosmetic identity so reports and the architecture map read consistently.
claims.why: This is a design intent statement; no code in this chunk verifies cosmetic usage.

claims.text: Return the shadow persona's call-name for (provider, role).
claims.why: The function takes provider and agent_name, looks up by_role, and returns the shadow name or default.

claims.text: All named workers on a lane: the per-role shadows plus any extra pool.
claims.why: The function combines values from by_role and pool keys and deduplicates.

observations.what: Module docstring claims shadow names are Chinese for DeepSeek and Mexican/Italian for Ollama, but this is not enforced in code; it depends on personas.json.
_registry is cached with lru_cache(maxsize=1); JSON file read once per process.
persona_for uses empty string as fallback for agent_name if None; by_role.get(None, ...) would not match if agent_name is None.
roster uses dict.fromkeys to deduplicate; order is preserved only in Python 3.7+.
